learningObjectives: Apply Data Transforms to copy, convert, and drive data using Run Data Transform automation or pre/post-processing actions.
Set default property values using the Data initialization page and understand the role of pyDefault and pySetFieldDefaults.

elements.text: Porter vs. translator — A porter carries a suitcase as-is (copy). A translator converts the message into another language (convert). A Data Transform does both: moves a value to a different field, or changes its data type entirely.

elements.description: Copies, converts and drives application data. It can calculate values, change formats and set defaults as well as copy between objects. Do not confuse setting or deriving a value with enforcing a blocking validation error.
Copies a field value into another field. Example: copy customer details from the checkout form into the shipping address fields.
Changes the data type of a value. Example: convert the string 'December 4, 2021' to the date value 12/04/2021. Data Transforms don't just copy — they convert too.

Consider references when later parent changes should remain available to a child. Use a copy when a snapshot or separately manipulated value is the actual requirement; reference is not mandatory for every parent-child field.
Added as an Automation Step in the Case Life Cycle. Runs automatically at runtime — no user interaction required. A new Data Transform can be defined inline (e.g., 'Convert string to date').
Configured on a Step's Pre/Post Processing tab. The Data Transform runs BEFORE the Step executes. Use case: populate fields before the form is displayed to the user.
The Data Transform runs AFTER the Step completes. Use case: clean up or convert data after the user submits a form.

elements.text: Pre-filled form at the doctor's office — when you arrive, the form already has your name, date of birth, and insurance details filled in. The Data initialization page works the same way: when a Case is created, fields arrive pre-populated with known values.

elements.term: Data initialization page — where to find it
elements.description: App Studio → Case Type → Settings tab → Data initialization. This is where you configure default property values assigned when a Case is created.
① Pre-populate user's First Name and Last Name from the OperatorID clipboard page. ② Set a date field to today's date. ③ Speed up iterative testing in development by pre-filling required fields.

elements.term: pyDefault and pySetFieldDefaults — when are they created?
elements.description: The first View creation described in this lesson generates pyDefault and pySetFieldDefaults. Distinguish this generation event from when each transform is later invoked.

elements.term: pyDefault vs pySetFieldDefaults — different trigger times
elements.description: Two built-in Data Transforms with different trigger points:
items: pyDefault — invoked when the Case is CREATED; calls pySetFieldDefaults as part of its logic
pySetFieldDefaults — runs each time a View is LOADED (can run multiple times per session)

elements.term: Best practice — Data init page for simple, pyDefault for complex
elements.description: Simple defaults → use the Data initialization page (it updates pyDefault). Complex default logic → edit pyDefault directly. Either way, never touch pySetFieldDefaults — it is system-managed and manual edits can be overwritten.

elements.description: The illustrated pyDefault example reads First Name and Last Name from the OperatorID Clipboard Page and declares that page on Pages & Classes. Follow that example without generalizing it into a rule that every Data Page reference must be declared or always fails at runtime without a declaration.

examPitfalls.title: Pre-processing vs. post-processing — order confusion
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks which Data Transform runs before an Assignment is presented vs. after it is submitted. Candidates reverse the order. Pre-processing Data Transforms run BEFORE the form is shown to the user; post-processing Data Transforms run AFTER the user submits.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Pre: runs BEFORE the Step executes. Post: runs AFTER the Step completes. 'Pre = before' is the mnemonic.

examPitfalls.title: Editing pySetFieldDefaults directly — system will overwrite it
examPitfalls.trapDescription: System updates during View configuration can overwrite manual pySetFieldDefaults changes. The lesson does not establish a named guardrail violation or regeneration on every save.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Simple defaults → use Data initialization page (updates pyDefault). Complex defaults → edit pyDefault directly. Never touch pySetFieldDefaults — it is system-managed and manual changes can be overwritten.

examPitfalls.title: Data initialization page is on the Settings tab — not the Data tab
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks where to configure the Data Transform that initializes a Case Type's default field values. Candidates navigate to the Data tab. This configuration is on the Case Type's Settings tab — not the Data tab.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Location: App Studio → Case Type → Settings tab → Data initialization. 'Settings' is the key word.

examPitfalls.title: pyDefault vs pySetFieldDefaults — who runs when?
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask when pyDefault runs vs. pySetFieldDefaults. Candidates say they are interchangeable. pyDefault runs when a new Case is created and sets general system defaults; pySetFieldDefaults runs when the Case Type's create form loads and sets field-specific default values.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: pyDefault runs when the Case is CREATED and invokes pySetFieldDefaults. pySetFieldDefaults runs every time a View is LOADED. Hierarchy: pyDefault (parent) → pySetFieldDefaults (child).

examPitfalls.title: Run Data Transform = Automation Step, not a user Step
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks how to run a Data Transform as part of the Case flow. Candidates describe adding a user Step. Data Transforms are executed via the 'Run Data Transform' Automation Step — they are not user-facing Steps and do not create Assignments.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Run Data Transform is an AUTOMATION Step — it executes automatically when the Case reaches that Step, with no user interaction.

examPitfalls.title: Data Transforms convert data types — not just copy
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what Data Transforms can do. Candidates say 'copy data between pages only.' Data Transforms can also convert data types (e.g., Text to Integer), apply conditions, iterate over page lists, and call other Data Transforms.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Data Transforms copy, convert, AND drive. Example: convert the string 'December 4, 2021' to a Date data type.

examPitfalls.title: Scope the page declaration to the illustrated reference
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not label every clipboard page a managed Data Page or infer that every missing declaration causes the same runtime failure.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: In the supplied OperatorID example, declare the page and its class on Pages & Classes before using its properties in the Data Transform.

Post-processing — runs the Data Transform after the Step completes
Run Data Transform Automation — add as a standalone Automation Step in the Case Life Cycle
Data initialization page — populates the summary field when the Case is created

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish capability, configured invocation, creation defaults and View configuration.

optionExplanations.B: Post-processing runs after, rather than preparing this form before presentation.
optionExplanations.C: A standalone automation is possible in a workflow but is not the Step-attached method requested.
optionExplanations.D: Creation defaults do not target preparation of this later form Step.

optionExplanations.B: The word only wrongly excludes the following automation invocation.
optionExplanations.C: Both described execution points can invoke the needed conversion transform.
optionExplanations.D: Creation initialization does not perform the later submitted-value conversion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer is configuring default property values for a new Case Type and wants to understand the execution order and purpose of pyDefault and pySetFieldDefaults. Which statement correctly describes the relationship between pyDefault and pySetFieldDefaults in Pega?

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish capability, configured invocation, creation defaults and View configuration.

optionExplanations.B: This reverses the containing invocation relationship.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega System Architect is explaining Data Transform capabilities and invocation patterns to a junior developer implementing data manipulation logic in a Claims application. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Data Transforms work in Pega?

optionExplanations.B: This incorrectly limits transforms to copying alone.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is explaining how Data Transforms are used for data manipulation in a Pega Case. Which TWO statements correctly describe Data Transform behavior?

A Data Transform can be invoked as a pre- or post-processing action on an Assignment or other automation step
A Data Transform executes automatically every time the Case page is loaded without any explicit invocation configured
A Data Transform can only set static default values and cannot read from external Data Pages or reference other properties

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish capability, configured invocation, creation defaults and View configuration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Transforms can manipulate and calculate values rather than being limited to static assignments. Pre/post-processing is one of the documented explicit invocation approaches.

optionExplanations.A: Transforms can manipulate and calculate values rather than being limited to static assignments.
optionExplanations.B: Pre/post-processing is one of the documented explicit invocation approaches.
optionExplanations.C: A transform does not run on every Case-page load merely because the Rule exists.
optionExplanations.D: The documented copying and references refute the proposed static-only restriction.
